reply_text:
*I’d block the merge on two findings* in `slug-validation` (`e8612a7`) vs `main`:

1. *[P1] Validation accepts a valid substring, not the whole slug* — `src/validate.js:1–4`  
   `/[a-z0-9-]+/` passes anything containing at least one allowed character. Confirmed that `"Hello"`, `"hello world"`, `"a/b"`, `"../admin"`, and `"a\n"` all pass and produce page URLs. `encodeURIComponent` encodes these inputs; it doesn’t enforce the slug policy.  
   *Recommendation:* enforce a whole-string match, including rejection of trailing line terminators—JavaScript’s `$` alone can match before a final newline.

2. *[P2] Reserved slugs aren’t enforced by the URL guard* — `src/route.js:3–5`  
   `pagePath` never calls `isReserved`. All four reserved names (`new`, `edit`, `admin`, `api`) produce URLs successfully, contrary to the README’s promise that they cannot be used for a page. Testing the reservation helper alone misses this integration gap.  
   *Recommendation:* reject reserved names in `pagePath` and test all four through that entry point.

*Verification:* all 4 existing tests pass, but the edge-case checks above reproduce both issues. Add rejection tests through `pagePath` for malformed and reserved slugs.

No code changed.
